title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
evaluated: Closed-set tasks PubHealth and ARC-Challenge; short-form QA PopQA and TriviaQA-unfiltered; long-form Bio generation (FactScore) and ASQA (str-em, MAUVE, citation precision/recall); baselines are LLMs with and without retrieval (ChatGPT, Llama2-chat, Alpaca, Llama2-FT etc.); training-scale ablation and a 50-sample human evaluation of plausibility/support and reflection-token reliability.
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH relative to the registry: current_registry_entry labels this 'defense: Self-RAG', but the paper evaluates NO attack, no poisoned or corrupted context, and no adversarial condition at all - it measures QA accuracy, factuality (FactScore) and citation precision on standard capability/factuality benchmarks. It is a non-adversarial fix (irrelevant/unhelpful retrieved passages, unsupported generation), not a defense. It is also borderline for the corpus: the untrustworthy-context aspect is only 'retrieved passages may be irrelevant or unsupported', which is adjacent to but weaker than context poisoning; belongs_in_corpus marked unsure for that reason. Close call between proposes_fix and improves_existing (it is a new named framework but squarely an extension of RAG). RULING: kept in corpus per screening decision.

title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management
evaluated: BrowseComp (36.2%), BrowseComp-ZH (47.3%), WideSearch-en Item-F1 (62.1%) and GAIA text-only (67.0%), against open-source agents (WebThinker, WebDancer, WebSailor, ASearcher, MiroThinker, WebExplorer, DeepDive, DeepDiver-V2, Kimi-K2, GLM-4.5, DeepSeek-V3.1) and proprietary agents (Claude-4-Sonnet/Opus, o4-mini, o3, OpenAI Deep Research); plus a context-dynamics analysis of 200 BrowseComp trajectories measuring average context token count and block count per turn.
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. this is one of the papers the screening brief warns about. The framing is 'context saturation as they accumulate noisy, raw histories' and 'critical signals become buried in noise', but nothing in the evaluation measures context degradation or context-induced error: the results tables are pure capability scores on information-seeking benchmarks (BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH, WideSearch, GAIA) and the only context-specific measurement is a token-count / block-count growth curve, i.e. an efficiency statistic. There is no ablation isolating noise or distraction. I therefore left contribution unsure (it would be proposes_fix if context saturation counts as an in-scope failure mode, and out_of_scope if, as the capability-only evaluation suggests, this is an agent-performance paper using 'context' in the capacity sense) and left technique_name/origin/parent_technique blank per the blank-means-no-decision rule. I disagree with the current registry entry, which records it as a proposed 'defense' - no adversary and no attack appear anywhere in the paper. Recommend a second pass decide between proposes_fix and out_of_scope. RULING: coded proposes_fix and kept in corpus per screening decision; the mismatch warning stands - nothing in the evaluation measures context degradation.

title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
evaluated: Multi-objective multi-hop QA composed from HotpotQA and Natural Questions (exact match, F1), open-domain web QA, and WebShop navigation (environment reward); accuracy baselines Search-R1, DeepResearcher, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Agent-FLAN, Agent-R, AgentLM; efficiency baselines a prompt-only agentic truncation variant and A-MEM; metrics peak token usage, average dependency length and inference time; RL vs SFT and format-reward ablations.
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. the same pattern as row 47. The introduction lists three motivations and only the third is in scope ('Overloaded and inefficient context. The accumulation of irrelevant or redundant content dilutes the model's attention.'); the other two, and the entire abstract, are inference cost, memory usage and out-of-distribution length generalisation. Every reported metric is task capability (EM, F1, environment reward) or efficiency (peak tokens, dependency length, inference time) - nothing measures attention dilution, distraction or any context-induced error. I left contribution unsure: out_of_scope is the reading the evaluation supports (agent capability/efficiency, 'long-horizon' in the capacity sense), proposes_fix only if the single dilution sentence is accepted as the paper's subject. technique_name/origin/parent_technique left blank per the blank-means-no-decision rule. I disagree with the current registry entry, which records MEM1 as a proposed 'defense' - the paper contains no adversary, no attack and no untrusted-content threat model. RULING: coded proposes_fix and kept in corpus per screening decision; the mismatch warning stands - every reported metric is capability or efficiency.

title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
evaluated: AppWorld (task completion score), OfficeBench (accuracy), Multi-objective QA / 8-objective QA (EM, F1); efficiency metrics are steps, average peak input tokens and dependency. Baselines: No Compression, FIFO, Retrieval, LLMLingua, naive Prompting compression. Agents/compressors: gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, and distilled Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-8B, Phi-4 compressors.
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper frames the problem as context dilution and 'reasoning degradation due to irrelevant information' / 'context distraction', and claims up to 46% improvement 'by mitigating context distraction', but nothing in the evaluation measures distraction, dilution or context rot directly. Section 4 measures only (a) task capability scores - AppWorld completion score, OfficeBench accuracy, 8-objective QA EM/F1 - and (b) efficiency - number of steps, average peak input tokens, dependency (KV cost), and compressor size after distillation. The distraction claim is inferred purely from accuracy going up when context is compressed for small models; there is no distractor-controlled experiment, no position/noise sweep, and no ablation isolating irrelevant content. Also disagrees with current_registry_entry: ACON is labelled 'defense' there, but there is no adversary anywhere in the paper - it is a non-adversarial fix (proposes_fix), so the registry entry should be reclassified.

title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
evaluated: LoCoMo (152/81/1307 train/val/test QA, adversarial subset excluded), MSC and LongMemEval; baselines LoCoMo RAG, A-Mem, Mem0, MemoryOS and a Memory-SFT behaviour-cloning variant; backbones LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct (3B-14B scales); metrics token-level F1, BLEU-1 and LLM-as-a-Judge on single-hop, multi-hop, open-domain and temporal questions.

DEFENSE-NAMES-style note: the only named artifact is the Memory-R1 framework (Memory Manager, Answer Agent, Memory Distillation). Registry entry 'defense: Memory-R1' is wrong in kind - it is a non-adversarial memory-management fix, not a defense against an attack.

evaluated: F1 on 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, PopQA and ComplexWebQuestions with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct, LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct; baselines Vanilla, Standard RAG, PRAG, PRAG-Combine; inference/training/storage cost comparison; RAGTruth benchmark with GPT-4o as judge comparing standard RAG vs DyPRAG-Combine; appendix analysis of contextual-vs-parametric knowledge conflict

Explicitly an extension of PRAG, so improves_existing, not the registry's 'proposed'. belongs_in_corpus marked unsure because the paper's core concern is RAG cost/efficiency and parametric knowledge injection rather than context becoming untrustworthy; the knowledge-conflict framing is what keeps it borderline in scope.

title: Memory as Action: Autonomous Context Curation for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
evaluated: Multi-objective HotpotQA-derived QA (up to 8 objectives, 200 samples/level), 2WikiMultihopQA, Bamboogle, HotpotQA, Musique, Frames, BrowseComp-Plus; baselines Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct full context, Sliding Window, Summarization, A-MEM, MEM1, Tongyi-DeepResearch, Search-R1; metrics task accuracy (LLM judge, three-pass consensus), solved sub-objective count, total tokens, tool-call frequency

title: Structurally Aligned Subtask-Level Memory for Software Engineering Agents
evaluated: SWE-bench Verified; mean Pass@1 against vanilla agents and instance-level memory baselines across multiple backbones (e.g., Gemini 2.5 Pro); ablation on number of interaction steps.

notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper frames itself around a context-contamination failure mode - instance-level memory retrieving globally similar but locally wrong experience, which 'can therefore introduce irrelevant guidance and mislead the agent' - but the evaluation measures ONLY task capability: Pass@1 resolution rate on SWE-bench Verified versus vanilla and instance-level-memory agents. No measurement of retrieval precision, of how often misguided retrieval occurs, or of any harm from the contaminated context itself; the mismatch is inferred only from aggregate task-score deltas. Registry entry names an 'UNNAMED: granularity mismatch' mechanism plus the method as a defense; I agree the failure mode is real but note the paper gives it only the lowercase descriptive phrase 'granularity mismatch', not a proper name other papers could cite, and it is a non-adversarial failure so 'fix' fits better than 'defense'.

title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control

Borderline in-scope: the untrustworthy content here is merely irrelevant, never planted.

title: The Cognitive Bandwidth Bottleneck: Shifting Long-Horizon Agent from Planning with Actions to Planning with Schemas
evaluated: Comparison of planning with actions (PwA) vs planning with schemas (PwS) across four interactive environments of increasing action-space size (ALFWorld ~35 actions, TextCraft, WebShop, SciWorld ~500 actions) measuring task success, plus a 'cognitive load stress test' that injects distractor actions into ALFWorld and varies model capacity to locate the representation-choice inflection point.

The paper is framed around context/cognitive overload - long action lists 'strain the context window' and create a decision bottleneck, and the Cognitive Bandwidth Perspective decomposes load into environment understanding, planning, schema instantiation and decision making - but every number reported is task success on capability benchmarks (ALFWorld, TextCraft, WebShop, SciWorld) plus the location of an inflection point; no measurement of attention, information loss or degradation from context length as such, and the authors themselves state the perspective is 'a qualitative lens rather than a measurable construct'. The distractor-injection stress test adds benign distractor actions, not untrusted content. Coded measurement_study because the contributions list leads with the systematic comparison and the conceptual perspective; PwS is an existing human-cognition-inspired paradigm the authors adopt rather than invent, so no technique_name. Registry lists 'mechanism: cognitive bandwidth bottleneck' and 'defense: Planning with Schemas (PwS)' - I disagree with calling PwS a defense (no adversary) and with treating the bottleneck as a measured failure mode.

title: CodeDelegator: Mitigating Context Pollution via Role Separation in Code-as-Action Agents
evaluated: tau^2-bench retail (115 tasks) and airline (50 tasks) pass^k for k=1..4, and MCPMark (127 tasks across Filesystem/GitHub/Notion/Playwright/PostgreSQL) pass@1, against ReAct and CodeAct baselines on DeepSeekV3.2 and GPT-5; ablation on MCPMark removing EPSS and removing role separation; plus a 50-task pilot study on CodeAct in the tau^2-Bench airline domain recording task success, final context length and cumulative code execution errors, stratified by official task success rate

notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper is framed around 'context pollution' (progressive dilution of task-relevant information by accumulated debugging traces), but the main evaluation (Sec. 5) measures only task capability: pass^k on tau^2-bench and pass@1 on MCPMark, plus component ablations in the same success-rate units. evaluated: CodeGym (12,800 training problems, 128-item held-out eval) with Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and BrowseComp-Plus (730 train / 100 eval, Qwen3-Embed-8B retriever) with Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct; baseline is vanilla multi-turn GRPO; metrics are task success rate / accuracy (+3.2% and +14.0% absolute) and working context length; ablations on overlong masking and advantage calculation, plus test-time scaling of the number of summarization rounds

evaluated: Code generation (HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, pass@1/pass@5), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, GSM-HARD accuracy), creative writing (win rate and TrueSkill human elo rating), embodied planning in Minecraft MC-TextWorld (executability and plausibility); baselines DIRECT, CoT, RAG 1-shot and RAG 5-shot; base models CodeLlama-7b, GPT-3.5, GPT-4

title: MemoBrain: Executive Memory as an Agentic Brain for Reasoning
evaluated: GAIA (103 text-only validation questions, L1-L3), WebWalkerQA (680 queries, easy/medium/hard), and BrowseComp-Plus (830 questions over a fixed candidate corpus with local dense retrieval). Baselines: direct reasoning (QwQ-32B, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1-671B), RAG variants (vanilla, query planning, iterative), and tool-integrated reasoning systems (ReAct, WebThinker, WebDancer, ReSum-GRPO, DeepAgent-RL, AgentFold, GLM-4.6, DeepResearch-30B-A3B). Metrics: Pass@1 accuracy and number of search calls. Ablations on design choices (w/o flush, w/o folding, delete, random drop), on memory-model size (MemoBrain-4B/8B/14B), and sensitivity to context budget from 8K to 128K - all reported as accuracy.
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper frames itself squarely around a context-trust/context-quality failure - accumulated reasoning traces and transient tool artifacts 'strain the bounded working context', 'allowing transient information to dominate and distract from task-relevant evidence, leading to cognitive overload and degraded task alignment' - but every number reported is capability: Pass@1 on GAIA, WebWalkerQA and BrowseComp-Plus, plus search-call counts. There is no measurement of distraction, of logical-continuity loss, of task-alignment drift, or of what fraction of pruned content was actually noise; the ablations (w/o flush, w/o folding, delete, random drop) and the 8K-128K context-budget sweep are also scored purely in accuracy, so they ablate the method's components rather than isolating the failure mode. The claimed mechanism - that MemoBrain removes distractors and preserves a high-salience backbone - is never measured directly. Keep in corpus; the note carries the warning. Registry disagreement: registry says 'defense: MemoBrain'. There is no adversary in this paper; the harmful context is the agent's own accumulated trace, so this is proposes_fix, not a defense. The paper also introduces 'executive memory' as a named paradigm, but it is a memory-architecture category rather than an attack or failure mode, so names_registry_technique is no.

title: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution

title: Beyond Compaction: Structured Context Eviction for Long-Horizon Agents

Partial mitigation worth recording: the matched context-budget design (Small 1950 / Large 2200) makes context composition the manipulated variable, and the method internally partitions tasks into an exogenous set (full history succeeds, structured fails = information loss) and an endogenous set (structured succeeds, full fails = hallucination / lost-in-the-middle mitigated) - but that partition is used inside the training feedback loop, not reported as an evaluation of the failure mode. REGISTRY DISAGREEMENT: registry says 'defense: HORMA'; no adversary is present, so proposes_fix.

title: SearchSwarm: Towards Delegation Intelligence in Agentic LLMs for Long-Horizon Deep Research

title: Beyond Entangled Planning: Task-Decoupled Planning for Long-Horizon Agents
evaluated: TravelPlanner (Delivery, commonsense and hard-constraint micro/macro pass rates, Final Pass), HotpotQA (Accuracy and Accurate Delivery, LLM-as-a-judge with Qwen-MAX) and ScienceWorld (environment reward), under two base models (DeepSeek-V3.2 and GPT-4o), against ReAct, CoT-with-initial-plan and Plan-and-Act. The reported gains are also modest and uneven: on ScienceWorld reward, TDP beats ReAct under GPT-4o (53.24 vs 50.63) but loses to it under DeepSeek-V3.2 (56.17 vs 58.26). REGISTRY DISAGREEMENT: current entry is 'defense: TDP (Task-Decoupled Planning)' with origin=proposed. title: G-MemLLM: Gated Latent Memory Augmentation for Long-Context Reasoning in Large Language Models

The 'w/o Perceive' ablation is a component ablation scored in EM (64.9 vs 65.3 on MathVista, 36.21 vs 39.40 on MAT-Search), not a measurement of the failure mode, and the top-k figure measures accuracy versus number of retrieved documents (noting that larger k 'may introduce noise') without quantifying the noise effect. title: Red-MIRROR: Agentic LLM-based Autonomous Penetration Testing with Reflective Verification and Knowledge-augmented Interaction
evaluated: XBOW benchmark (50 web exploitation challenges) and Vulhub CVE scenarios; baselines PentestAgent (50.0%), AutoPT (46.0%) and VulnBot (6.0%); metrics are overall exploitation success rate (86.0%), subtask completion rate (93.99%), Time-To-Exploit in agent steps (21.77 -> 13.19 on XBOW) and average dollar token cost per challenge ($0.10 -> $0.20); four-configuration ablation isolating SRMM and Dual-phase Reflection
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper's stated failure modes are context failures - 'fragmented session memory', 'memory fragmentation', 'over-reliance on parametric knowledge' and 'payload hallucination in long-horizon attacks' - but the evaluation measures only capability and efficiency: exploitation success rate and subtask completion on XBOW and Vulhub, Time-To-Exploit in agent steps, and dollar cost per challenge. The RQ3 ablation toggles SRMM and Dual-phase Reflection on and off but still scores them by solve rate and TTE; memory fragmentation, state loss across agents and hallucinated payloads are never measured directly. DEFENSE-NAMES: Red-MIRROR; Shared Recurrent Memory Mechanism (SRMM); Dual-Phase Reflection. Coded proposes_fix because the named failure is non-adversarial (the agent losing its own state), not an attacker planting content; the offensive subject matter is the target web app, not the LLM's context. Worth flagging for the SoK: Section 3.2 runs a STRIDE-style self-analysis of the pentest agent itself and claims SRMM's immutable write-once semantics plus gated RAG counter memory tampering and information disclosure, and that Dual-Phase Reflection's hard 10-iteration cap prevents reflection-loop DoS - a context-poisoning threat model stated but, like the rest, never empirically tested. No current_registry_entry.

title: QUITO-X: A New Perspective on Context Compression from the Information Bottleneck Theory
evaluated: Nine datasets - CoQA, Quoref, and LongBench's 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA, MuSiQue, TriviaQA and Gov_Report - at compression ratios 1.00/0.75/0.50/0.25/0.00, scored by Exact Match (ROUGE-L for Gov_Report) with LongChat-13B-16k and LLaMA3-8B-Instruct readers; baselines are Selective Context, LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua2 and QUITO; also reports compression rate and memory usage.

There is no position-controlled or distractor-controlled experiment, no measurement of where in the context the needed evidence sits, and no quantification of dilution - so 'lost in the middle' is asserted in the introduction and never measured. DEFENSE-NAMES (mitigation name, non-adversarial): QUITO-X. title: STAR-PólyaMath: Multi-Agent Reasoning under Persistent Meta-Strategic Supervision
evaluated: Eight competition mathematics benchmarks - AIME 2025, AIME 2026, MathArena Apex Shortlist, MathArena Apex 2025, Putnam 2025, IMO 2025, HMMT February 2026, USAMO 2026 - scored by answer correctness or human proof rubric, against GPT-5.5/5.4/5.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus 4.7/4.6, DeepSeek-v4-Pro, DeepSeek-v3.2-Speciale, Kimi K2.6/K2.5 and GLM 5.1; plus ablations substituting backbones and removing components, also scored on the same benchmarks.

None of the three failure modes is measured directly: no hallucination-propagation rate, no context-length or memory-retention analysis, no distractor or contradictory-update probe. The ablations only show that removing a component lowers benchmark accuracy, which is still capability-only evidence. DEFENSE-NAMES (mitigation names, non-adversarial): STAR-PolyaMath; persistent Meta-Strategist; challenge-step-replan loop; trace-back; Reasoner-Verifier logic/goal gates. REGISTRY DISAGREEMENT: current entry 'defense: STAR-PolyaMath' is wrong on two counts - there is no adversary anywhere in the paper, and the artifact is a reasoning-orchestration framework, so proposes_fix. Registry entry was empty; benchmark_or_dataset with names_registry_technique=no is the correct coding (the paper names task categories such as Object Location Memory and Timeline Reconstruction, not attacks or failure modes that other papers test against). Partial alignment: Table 2 reports accuracy as a function of temporal certification length and the error taxonomy isolates Visual Omission, so degradation with context span is measured indirectly, but no distractor-controlled ablation or direct failure-mode measurement exists. title: Agentic Cloud Decoys: A Deception-Driven Framework for Autonomous Intrusion Investigation
evaluated: Ten controlled AWS S3 decoy scenarios (enumeration only, enumeration+retrieval, multi-object retrieval, denied access, destructive deletion, delayed access, and scripted/SDK variants), scored manually by the authors against driver-script ground truth on complete event coverage, correct ordering, correct attribution of IAM principal/access key/role chain, complete object naming, and unsupported assertions; plus end-to-end latency (four to five minutes). Suite score 9.5/10, nine of ten scenarios reconstructed completely, zero untraceable assertions. The authors state there is no baseline, no ablation, no independent scoring, and one service on one provider - and NO prompt-injection experiment at all
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The abstract names adversary-authored cloud telemetry (attacker-chosen S3 object keys and user-agent strings that CloudTrail records verbatim) as turning any log-to-prompt path into an indirect prompt injection channel that a decoy actively widens, but the evaluation measures only investigation capability and efficiency: scenario-level reconstruction accuracy (event coverage, ordering, IAM attribution, object naming, unsupported assertions) and end-to-end latency. No injection payload is ever planted in a decoy bucket and no injection resistance is measured. This is an unusually honest instance - the authors themselves declare the exposure unaddressed and the prototype non-mitigating - but the marker is still correct: the context-poisoning claim is stated and not measured. DEFENSE-NAMES: Cloud Decoy AI Agent; session aggregation operator over a four-element pivot tuple of provider-derived fields; dynamic prompt generation (two-stage prompt assembly enforcing a stated grounding invariant, Invariant 1). Defense-only paper, so names_registry_technique=no; it coins no attack name, reusing 'indirect prompt injection'. Belongs in the corpus as a clear articulation of a poisoning channel (attacker-controlled fields in provider logs, with the decoy as an adversary-controlled write surface feeding the analysis path) even though it is unmeasured. Other weaknesses the authors admit: self-scored, no baseline, no ablation, one provider. No current registry entry.

title: Z-Space: A Multi-Agent Tool Orchestration Framework for Enterprise-Grade LLM Automation
evaluated: Self-constructed enterprise dataset of 541 KBT tools and 280 user instructions (single- to six-step), with Qwen-plus/Qwen-max; baselines are an all-injection LLM baseline and an LLM+RAG baseline; metrics are tool invocation accuracy, token consumption and planning success rate, plus a scalability sweep of tool counts from 20 to 520 measuring token consumption
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper frames the problem as context inflation and attention dilution from injecting thousands of tool descriptions ('drowns critical semantic cues in massive redundant information, dispersing model attention'), but the evaluation measures only capability and efficiency: tool invocation accuracy (92% vs 82.95% LLM+RAG vs 27.32% LLM), token consumption (-96.26%) and planning success rate, plus token-count scaling as the tool repository grows. There is no distractor-controlled ablation isolating dilution, and no adversary anywhere in the paper. Non-adversarial context-management method, hence proposes_fix (FSWW fused subspace weighted tool filtering is the component algorithm). Registry entry was empty; note that this would be a 'defense:' mislabel candidate since no attacker exists.

title: CoMIC: Collaborative Memory and Insights Circulation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Cloud-Edge Systems
evaluated: Five long-horizon tasks requiring 20+ steps (Blocksworld, Gripper, Tyreworld, Barman, Jericho) with Mistral-7b edge agents and deepseek-chat as cloud critic, in a homogeneous (Scenario A) and heterogeneous GPT-4-turbo/Mistral-7b (Scenario B) setup; baselines are STANDARD (AgentBoard-adapted memory agent) and LOCAL (HiAgent); metrics are Success Rate, Progress Rate, Grounding Accuracy, execution Steps, context token consumption, plus cloud-side coordination and overhead metrics
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper is framed around context explosion and growing prompt context from concatenating entire interaction histories, but the evaluation measures capability and efficiency only: Success Rate, Progress Rate, Grounding Accuracy, step count and context token consumption (-27.88%) on symbolic planning and text-game tasks. There is no distractor-controlled or noisy-history ablation isolating the context-saturation failure, and no adversary anywhere. Non-adversarial context-management method (hierarchical subgoal memory with selective re-expansion plus a cloud critic), hence proposes_fix. Registry entry was empty; this is the kind of paper that would be mislabelled 'defense:' despite having no attacker.

title: ToolSelf: Unifying Task Execution and Self-Reconfiguration via Tool-Driven Emergent Adaptation
evaluated: FRAMES, xbench, GAIA, GAIA(WS) WebSailor subset, SWE-bench Lite, with Qwen3-8B/14B; baselines Vanilla Agent, OpenHands, WebSailor, SWE-Agent, Co-Sight, SWE-Search, AutoAgent, OWL, ReSum, OAgents, AgenTRIM; plus CAT training ablation (RFT, RFT+KTO)
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper frames part of its problem as context dilution and makes the context-management mode m (how history is maintained, compressed, truncated, organized) one of the five runtime-reconfigurable configuration dimensions, but the evaluation measures ONLY end-task capability: pass rates on FRAMES, xbench, GAIA, GAIA(WS) and SWE-bench Lite, plus a training ablation (CAT: RFT then KTO). Nothing measures context quality, history noise, distraction, truncation loss, or any context-related failure mode; there are no token/latency measurements in the main results either. Borderline scope: the paper's dominant framing is static-vs-dynamic agent configuration (capability/planning), so it could arguably be out_of_scope, but per Ruling 1 it is kept in the corpus as a proposes_fix with this marker. No adversary anywhere. Secondary named component: Configuration-Aware Two-stage Training (CAT). No registry entry to disagree with.

title: SmoothAgent: Efficient Long-Horizon LLM-Based Agent Serving with Lookahead Context Engineering
evaluated: Synchronous context engineering as the baseline, across four strategies (offloading, keep-recent-K, summarization, sub-agent isolation), on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B H100 deployments in both PD co-located and PD-disaggregated settings at concurrency 1-64; also integrated into LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen and OpenClaw. Every reported metric is systems efficiency: tail and transform-point time-to-first-token (up to 11.9x improvement, 64.5% average reduction under disaggregation), context length per turn, and KV-cache re-prefill cost. No accuracy, task-success or quality metric is reported anywhere.
notes: CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH. The paper motivates itself on context rot - 'models often suffer from context rot [22], where performance degrades as the context becomes longer and noisier' - and on context engineering existing to mitigate it, but the evaluation measures ONLY serving efficiency: transform-point and tail TTFT, context length over turns, and KV-cache re-prefill overhead on Qwen3-8B/32B. Model quality, answer accuracy and task success are never measured, so the claim that context engineering 'improves agent accuracy and robustness' is assumed, not tested. Quote note on the evidence_quote: the source renders the multiplication sign as a times symbol; it is transcribed here as 'x' in '11.9x'. Caveat on names_registry_technique: 'context rot' is cited from reference [22], not coined here; 'context transformation overhead' is the paper's own named non-adversarial failure, though it is a performance overhead rather than a correctness failure mode, so this is the softer end of 'yes'. No adversary anywhere in the paper. No current_registry_entry, so no disagreement to record.
